answer: A reputation vault that only unlocks at an agent's zenith of verified work resists Sybils by making identity expensive to fake. Each agent keeps an atlas of signed attestations from independent peers; new identities start with zero history, so an attacker must pay real compute and time for every fake account before it can transact. Because reputation accrues slowly and decays when idle, flooding the network with cheap clones yields no trust, while honest agents compound theirs.
